episodes.215955: A surface trough initiated widely scattered thunderstorms. One cluster made it to the upper tidal Potomac River, and produced localized gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.216023: A strong upper high was over the south central U.S. on August 31st. Southerly flow on the western side of the upper high combined with a disturbance over the Great Basin and Four Corners helped funnel up monsoon moisture across western and central New Mexico. This higher moisture combined with modest daytime heating resulted in the development of showers and thunderstorms across central New Mexico mainly during the afternoon and evening hours. Storms produced flash flooding in Escobosa on the east slopes of the Manzano Mountains, Chimayo, and on Trigo Springs Road on the west slopes of the Manzano Mountains. Additionally, storms produced severe wind gusts at the Black Mesa RAWS near Espanola and Albuquerque International Sunport due to wet microbursts. Thunderstorms slowly tapered off during the late evening hours.
episodes.216918: A line of thunderstorms produced high winds across portions of north central South Dakota, with a peak wind gust of 66 mph measured at the South Dakota State University mesonet station near Timber Lake.
episodes.216949: A strong thunderstorm produced frequent lightning over Quebradillas on August 31st.
episodes.217221: As high pressure moved eastwards away from the Intermountain West, newly-established southwesterly flow brought another surge of moisture through the southwestern United States. A passing shortwave supported stronger storm development. This left some locations prone to strong outflow gusts in spite of the more saturated low-level atmosphere. Many storms also produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning. Some strikes caused damage across west-central Colorado.
episodes.217347: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the mid to late afternoon across portions of La Paz County, just north of I-10 with another area of thunderstorms affecting much of south-central AZ from northern Pinal County through much of Maricopa County, including the Phoenix metro area, during the evening hours. The cluster of storms that affected much of south-central AZ developed along a strong outflow boundary that emanated from a separate storm complex over Pima County. The environment these thunderstorms developed under was characterized by MLCAPE values ranging between 1000-2000 J/KG as well as increased upper-level ascent from an approaching upper trough. With DCAPE values exceeding 1000 J/KG, strong to severe downburst wind gusts were observed with the strongest storms and high rainfall rates in excess 1-2 per hour resulted in isolated instances of flash flooding.
episodes.217516: During the afternoon hours, a cluster of severe thunderstorms developed across portions of La Paz County in an area between the towns of Quartzsite, Salome, and Bouse. These thunderstorms were fueled by MLCAPE values in excess of 1000 J/KG along with upper-level support from a shortwave trough traversing the Great Basin Region. With rainfall rates in excess of 2/hr, there were several reports of flash flooding in Bouse as well as portions of Quartzsite as overflowing washes inundated low-water crossings. There were also reports of damaging winds, especially in Bouse, with downed power poles and an RV trailer severely damaged.
episodes.217685: A trough extending from a low in Canada provided weak forcing across the area during the early morning hours. One storm that went through Oakley produced penny size hail in town according to Emergency Management.
episodes.217877: A deep low pressure trough over the Great Basin with favorable upper level jet support draped across Utah allowed for stronger thunderstorm activity. Deep monsoonal moisture in place, in addition to the stronger storms, resulted in more widespread heavy rainfall and multiple rounds of storms with numerous flash flooding and debris flows across western Colorado and eastern Utah.
episodes.218191: A sharp frontal boundary progressed east across the state during the early afternoon and evening, with thunderstorms developing in an unstable atmosphere. The environment primarily favored a severe wind threat, with numerous reports of damaging thunderstorm wind gusts across western and parts of south central North Dakota. The most concentrated area of damage and strongest estimated wind gusts was in the Hettinger area in Adams County. Winds were estimated up to 75 mph with minor roof damage, downed trees, and a downed powerline near the Hettinger High School football field.
episodes.218225: A weak frontal boundary slowing dropping southward into southern Georgia was the main driving force behind scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, including isolated strong to severe thunderstorms during this period, along with the usual interactions with sea breeze/outflow interactions during strong diurnal heating. Many areas received 2+ inches or more of rainfall during this period thanks to very high available moisture and slow storm motion, though a report of isolated severe thunderstorm damage also occurred with this episode.
episodes.218260: A line of thunderstorms moved across the region and brought damaging wind gusts to much of western SD.
episodes.218480: With the subtropical ridge remaining in place, a stronger trough would impact the Pacific Northwest resulting in more widespread flash flooding across southern and central Utah, as well as widespread severe weather across the majority of Utah. This would go on to produce a prolific wind-driven hail event in Lynndyl, Utah.
episodes.218538: A singular cluster of strong to localized severe thunderstorms developed across eastern Colorado and tracked into western Kansas. A lone severe wind gust was measured in Kearny County as storms moved through the county.
episodes.218567: A weakening upper trough coupled and surface disturbance over the central Gulf favored an environment supportive of convection that produced strong marine wind gusts over the Tampa Bay area waters.
episodes.218581: Monsoon moisture resulted in an isolated thunderstorm in Mohave County in northwestern Arizona that produced hail.
episodes.218582: Monsoon moisture brought showers and thunderstorms to Lincoln County in southern Nevada that resulted in hail and flash flooding.

events.narrative: Lightning struck a tree which subsequently fell onto nearby powerlines on the evening of August 30. The powerlines fell across 17 1/2 Rd., closing the road in both directions.

Grand Junction Parks and Recreation reported mud covering the Riverfront Trail and portions of sidewalks along Monument Road in several locations and flooding at river underpasses due to heavy rainfall.

events.county: Tidal Potomac Key Bridge To Indian Hd Md
events.narrative: A thunderstorm produced an estimated wind gust to 34 knots (39 MPH) near the ASOS at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (KDCA) adjacent to the tidal Potomac River.
Tatanka Prairie mesonet station reported wind gusts up to 65 mph.
Reported at this location.
I-70 closed down due to multiple mudslides at Mile Markers 72, 75, and 105. Start time is estimated from radar.

Heavy rainfall caused strong flow in West Creek along Highway 141. This led to mud spilling out over the roadway with the most significant impacts noted at Mile Marker 115 and traffic also being turned around at Mile Marker 122. The highway did not reopen until approximately 8:00 PM MDT on July 31. Start time is estimated from radar.
A thunderstorm gust of 66 mph was measured at the Delta Blake Field Airport at approximately 6:55 PM MDT. No reports of injuries, damages, or fatalities were received in association with this event.
A trained spotter estimated wind gusts up around 60 mph.
Downed power poles in the area of Palm Drive to Old Bell Road and Mesquite Avenue to Salome Road in Salome. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 60 mph. No injuries reported.

A montage of images showed significant wind damage in Salome, including several large downed trees, roof parts blown off, and a damaged garage door. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards 60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
One inch hail reported in Havasu Heights.
Couple of vehicles had to be pulled out of the wash located near the area of Salome and Centennial Park Roads in Salome. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

Fence fell over along with roof damage at a property located approximately 3 miles east of North Branding Iron Road and Barnes Road in Maricopa. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

Roof collapse reported at a property located along North Lavern Lane just north of Papago Road in Maricopa. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

Several damaged animal enclosures and downed trees were reported at the Gud Ark Animal Sanctuary located in Maricopa. The animal enclosures that were damaged had the roof collapse and flipped on its side. One bird enclosure flipped over in about 1 foot of water, trapping and drowning seven birds.  Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 70 mph, as measured from a Davis Weather Station located nearby. Timing estimated from radar.

A large food trailer was knocked over on its side at the Maricopa Pantry located near the area of Ralston and Papago Roads in Maricopa. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 70 mph, as measured by a Davis Weather Station located nearby. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
A public personal Ambient Weather Network station measured a 62 knot wind gust with thunderstorms.

An animal sanctuary located in the area of Deer Valley Road and North 223rd Avenue in Surprise suffered structural damage. A shed used to store hay was destroyed, a fencing line was knocked down, and there was partial roof damage to the animal shelters. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. According to the sanctuary owner, total damage was estimated at approximately $15,000.

Very large tree uprooted with at least one other smaller tree downed along with a number of branches at the Glendale Community College located in Glendale. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

Significant wind damage was observed along the Sonoran Gate Community located in the area of Dove Valley Road from North Valley Parkway to Cave Creek Road down to Sonoran Desert Drive in North Phoenix. 59 downed trees of different sizes, including considerable damage to numerous large palo verde trees were reported. 15 homes having roof damage, including shingles/tiles peeled off, were also reported. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Stream Gauge along Daggs Wash near Peak View Road in Wittmann showed water levels rising above the alarm stage level of 1.5 feet, peaking at 2.19 feet (649 cfs) and likely impacting low water-crossings just upstream, including Dixileta Drive. Timing estimated based on the period water levels rose above and then receded below alarm stage. No damages or injuries reported.
Hail around dime/penny size in Oakley. Dispatch also reported sub-severe (<1 inch) hail briefly covered the roads, but quickly melted from rain.
A 429 cfs flood wave was reported by the USGS gauge at US-89.

Paria Contact Station reported flash flooding in Buckskin Gulch from early morning heavy rain. Flood waters deposited mud and boulders on House Rock Valley road leading into Buckskin parking area, limiting access.
Personal weather station Dads - KGABRUNS102 measured 2.81 inches of rain in the past  hour. Surrounding sites measured 1-2.5  inches.
Gauge on upper Pine Creek showed a flash flood wave around 171 cfs heading down the  drainage toward the Escalante River.
River Gauge on the Escalante at Escalante indicates a 433 cfs flood wave hit the gauge at 1025.
Goblin Valley State Park reported high flows out of slot canyons along Little Wildhorse Road before Little Wildhorse Slot Canyon.
Severe flooding in Springdale. SR-9 is reported impassible in parts of Springdale.
Gauge at the North Fork of the Virgin River at Springdale rose to 2000 cfs and continued to increase.
Large flood wave reported on the East Fork of the Virgin River Gauge, 1000 cfs and continued to increase.
One inch hail reported at Kershaw-Ryan State Park.

According to reports from broadcast media, a residence in Las Talas, Quebradillas, was struck by lightning. The strike caused electrical service disruptions and structural damage to the house ceiling, resulting in portions of it collapsing.
Water running across SR-21 near mile post 104.
Heavy rain from an isolated storm caused a mudslide that covered the westbound lanes of Highway 64 near Mile Point 61.1. Start time is estimate from radar.
Large flood wave moving down Pine Creek toward the Escalante River. Currently at 1090 cfs and rising.
USGS guage shows the Escalante River peaked at 2560 CFS. As of 525 PM the gauge was rising again at around 2200 CFS.
Piute County Emergency Management reported flooding and debris flow in the Deer Creek  drainage within the Silver King burn scar. This led to several washed out road crossings.
Emergency manager reported flooding near Cannonville that compromised the town water  supply.
Piute County Emergency Management reported flooding and an associated closure of Highway 89 originating from heavy rain and flooding in the City Creek drainage in the Cottonwood burn scar.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across State Route 319 near the Utah border.
Mesonet station UTLMP Lampson Canyon reported a severe wind gust to 60 mph.
Mesonet station PC349 Nephi West reported a severe wind gust to 59 mph.
WeatherFlow site XTAM Tampa Bay Cut J reported a 45 mph wind gust.
ASOS site KSPG Albert Whitted Airport reported a 43 mph wind gust.
Plomosa Road impassable from approximately Mile Marker 12 to Bouse due to flooding, including within the vicinity of Bouse Wash. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Video showed Yellow Bird Drive a Bouse Wash in Bouse impassable due to flooding. No damage or injuries reported.
Photos showed downed power poles along Avenue 42E near Mile Marker 7 in Bouse. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 70 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

Photos showed an RV trailer overturned and severely damaged near the area of 42E and Mile Marker 8 in Bouse. Peak wind gusts were estimated upwards of 70 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
PORTS site MTBF1 Middle Tampa Bay reported a 47 mph wind gust.
WeatherFlow site XSSN Sunshine Skyway North reported a 41 mph wind gust.
Swift water rescue performed at Joshua Drive along Bouse wash due to overflowing water from the wash. No injuries reported.
WeatherFlow site XSKY Skyway Fishing Pier reported a 41 mph wind gust.
Flooding reported on State Route 72 eastbound near Joshua Drive in Bouse. No damages or injuries reported.
Video on social media shows a very large flood on Calf Creek, with portions of the campground inundated by floodwaters. Calf Creek was well out of bank. Time estimated based on radar.
Capitol Reef National Park reported flows on Sulphur Creek and Capitol Gorge due to  steady rainfall, described as gentler rises as opposed to flash flooding.

Bernalillo County emergency manager shared a video from an unknown source of severe flooding in a ditch along NM 337 near Filomeno Road. Floodwaters can be seen overflowing this ditch and onto part of NM 337 in front of the entrance to a private ranch.
The Black Mesa RAWS measured a 58 mph wind gust due to a wet microburst.
Video shared from Facebook shows floodwaters in the Arroyo de Los Alamos crossing NM 76 at mile marker 7 making the road impassible and disrupting traffic on the highway.
Videos of flash flooding where Birch Creek enters into the Escalante River.
